case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 154 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 17:15:34Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, but the provider still signs its webhooks with the secret it used before. Since that deploy, the receiver rejects every provider webhook with HTTP 400 'signature mismatch'. Nothing is acknowledged or put on provider-events, so the provider keeps retrying and the backlog grows. Because nothing reaches the ledger or payment-confirmer, the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff, and BooksBehindProvider fires with 154 webhooks unacknowledged. The bad_signature rate keeps rising because retries add to the new webhooks. Left open: the tools cannot show the provider's current signing secret or which version the receiver ran before. I am inferring from the timing and the mismatch that the previous version matches the provider's.

evidence.shows: webhook-receiver is the only service changed recently: recreated at 17:15:34Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, after the rest of the stack came up at 17:14:08Z and about 50 s before the alert at 17:16:22Z.
Every recent POST /webhooks/provider returns 400 with the WARNING 'webhook refused: bad signature', reason 'signature mismatch'. No webhook is accepted.

Before 17:15:34, webhooks were 'queued' at about 1-3/s with no bad_signature. After the deploy, bad_signature appears (4.8/s at 17:15:54) and climbs to 22/s as retries pile up, while queued decays to zero (no point after 17:16:14).
A query filtered on ERROR/WARN found nothing because the receiver logs these refusals at level WARNING, so this result does not contradict the others.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its previous settings, which restores the earlier WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION that the provider still signs with. The provider retries until it gets an acknowledgment, so the refused webhooks should be redelivered, queued and processed. Afterwards, run money_check (wait=true) to confirm the books settle. Redo the secret rotation only once the provider signs with the v2 secret, or once the receiver accepts both secrets during the cutover.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only webhook-receiver is recreated, and it is down for a few seconds while it restarts. Webhooks sent in that time fail and are retried by the provider. After the rollback, the retry backlog arrives as a burst. ledger-consumer runs the idempotent handler and payment-confirmer runs by_our_id, so duplicate deliveries should not double-book, but the consumers will see brief lag. If v2 was meant to answer a compromised v1 secret, the rollback re-accepts webhooks signed with v1.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If webhooks are still refused after the rollback, or if v2 is required for security, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2 and coordinate with the provider to switch its signing secret, ideally with the receiver accepting both secrets during the cutover. The provider keeps retrying, so no webhook is lost while this is sorted out.
